stem: A 58-year-old man presents with 4 hours of central chest pain. His ECG shows no ST-segment elevation. At 6 hours after symptom onset, high-sensitivity troponin I is elevated, while CK-MB remains normal. Based on these findings, what is the most likely diagnosis?
keywords: “ECG shows no ST-segment elevation” – Rules out STEMI, points toward NSTEMI or unstable angina.
“High-sensitivity troponin I is elevated” – Confirms myocardial injury; distinguishes NSTEMI from unstable angina.

B.title: Confirms NSTEMI
B.body:
NSTEMI is diagnosed when there is myocardial injury evidenced by elevated cardiac biomarkers (troponin) without ST-segment elevation on ECG.
This patient has elevated high-sensitivity troponin I at 6 hours, CK-MB normal, and no ST-elevation, which fits NSTEMI criteria.
Key point: Troponin is more sensitive than CK-MB and rises earlier in myocardial injury. NSTEMI can be diagnosed even if CK-MB is normal.

A.title: Confirms STEMI
A.body:
STEMI requires ST-segment elevation on ECG or new LBBB.
In this patient, ECG is normal, so STEMI is not present.

C.title: Suggests unstable angina
C.body:
Unstable angina presents with chest pain at rest or new-onset, normal ECG or nonspecific changes, and no rise in cardiac biomarkers.
This patient has elevated troponin, so UA is excluded.

D.title: Indicates pericarditis
D.body:
Pericarditis often presents with diffuse ST-elevation, PR depression, and chest pain that changes with posture.
Biomarkers may be mildly elevated but usually not isolated troponin rise without ECG changes.

E.title: Excludes ACS
E.body: Elevated troponin confirms myocardial injury, so ACS cannot be excluded.

keyConcept: NSTEMI is diagnosed in patients with elevated cardiac biomarkers (troponin) without ST-segment elevation. High-sensitivity troponin is more sensitive than CK-MB. Unstable angina occurs with normal biomarkers, and STEMI requires ECG changes.

metadata.subtopic: Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) - STEMI vs NSTEMI (Pathophysiology & Biomarkers)

classicTriad: Chest pain + normal ECG + elevated troponin → Classic triad for NSTEMI.
differentialDiagnosisTableName: Acute Coronary Syndrome – NSTEMI Differential Diagnosis of NSTEMI

featureTable.description: Myocardial ischemia with elevated cardiac biomarkers but no ST-segment elevation on ECG
featureTable.clinicalImportance: Differentiates NSTEMI from STEMI and unstable angina

featureTable.description: Central chest pain, often at rest or minimal exertion, may radiate to arm/jaw/back, associated with sweating, nausea
Normal or nonspecific ST/T changes, no ST elevation
High-sensitivity troponin I/T elevated, CK-MB may be normal or mildly raised
Hypertension, diabetes, smoking, dyslipidemia, older age, male sex
Antiplatelets (aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitor), anticoagulants, beta-blockers, statins, early invasive strategy if high risk
Heart failure, arrhythmias, recurrent ischemia, cardiogenic shock

differentialDiagnosisTable.distinguishingFeatures: Chest pain at rest or minimal exertion
differentialDiagnosisTable.keyDifferences: No elevation of cardiac biomarkers; ECG may show ST depression or T-wave inversion

differentialDiagnosisTable.distinguishingFeatures: Chest pain with ST-segment elevation on ECG
differentialDiagnosisTable.keyDifferences: ECG shows ST elevation, usually higher troponin rise

differentialDiagnosisTable.distinguishingFeatures: Chest pain, viral prodrome, sometimes fever
differentialDiagnosisTable.keyDifferences: Troponin elevated, ECG may show diffuse ST changes; cardiac MRI may help

differentialDiagnosisTable.distinguishingFeatures: Sharp chest pain, relieved by leaning forward
differentialDiagnosisTable.keyDifferences: ECG shows diffuse ST elevation and PR depression, biomarkers may be mildly raised

differentialDiagnosisTable.distinguishingFeatures: Sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, hypoxia
differentialDiagnosisTable.keyDifferences: Troponin may rise, ECG may show S1Q3T3 pattern, imaging confirms PE

differentialDiagnosisTable.distinguishingFeatures: Sudden severe tearing chest/back pain, pulse deficit
differentialDiagnosisTable.keyDifferences: Troponin may rise; CT angiography shows dissection
Troponin may rise due to demand ischemia; ECG and echo help differentiate

diagram.name: NSTEMI (Non–ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction)
diagram.caption: This diagram illustrates the pathophysiology of NSTEMI, showing partial coronary artery occlusion leading to subendocardial ischemia and myocardial necrosis. It highlights key clinical features, ECG findings (no ST elevation with possible ST depression/T-wave inversion), and the role of elevated troponin in diagnosis, along with an overview of initial management strategies.
